reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes joining Forsage and presents partner, team and ratio metrics alongside claimed profits, then urges viewers to try to make similar income and contact the promoter. The combination of recruitment-oriented program claims, income promotion and direct contact solicitation supports a tiered recruitment mechanism rather than an ordinary financial demonstration.

citations.quote: See here mine made at 925 L, so u also try to make such income SO CALL ME, MAIL ME

opening.argument: Judge the income claim by what it actually says. The speaker describes an amount as their own and invites viewers to check the calculation: “See here mine made at 925 L.” That is a personal claim, not an explicit promise that viewers will earn the same amount. Even “so u also try to make such income” says try, not that success is assured. The video may be promotional, but the cited words do not establish a guaranteed return or a completed payout to anyone who joins.

citations.quote: Then I'll insert my amount in front of you, so u can also check
See here mine made at 925 L, so u also try to make such income SO CALL ME, MAIL ME

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats a displayed profile and its partner and team fields as proof of a tiered earning mechanism. Those fields are visible, but the sampled screen does not explain how either field generates income. The speaker's invitation to try and to make contact is promotional; it still does not state that joining guarantees the displayed result.

citations.quote: so u also try to make such income SO CALL ME, MAIL ME

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An explicit guarantee is not necessary to understand the pitch. The title offers instructions for joining Forsage, while the speaker pairs a large personal income claim with an invitation to try for similar income and contact them. The visible profile places profits beside partner and team metrics. Reading “try” as uncertainty does not erase that recruitment-oriented presentation.

citations.quote: See here mine made at 925 L, so u also try to make such income SO CALL ME, MAIL ME

opening.argument: This can be read as a walkthrough of what the speaker is doing on screen. The title begins “How to join,” the speaker says they will check an amount using Binance and show their own amount so viewers can check, and the sampled frames move from a Forsage profile to a BUSD purchase form. Those are concrete demonstration steps. The income claim deserves scrutiny, but the material shown does not establish that a viewer joined, paid the speaker, or received any promised return.

citations.quote: now check it how much this 1000 Rs is made with Binance then i'll check how much this 10 L is made with NIRV Then I'll insert my amount in front of you, so u can also check

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to the profile's partner, team, ratio and profit fields, but showing a dashboard is also consistent with explaining an interface. Its figures do not, by themselves, show a payment from a recruit or explain the source of the listed profits. The contact invitation may offer further help with the process rather than establish a completed recruitment transaction.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can also be promotion. Here, “How to join” directs viewers toward participation, while the speaker urges them to seek similar income and contact them. The dashboard displays profits together with partner and team counts, and the later BUSD purchase form gives the walkthrough a transaction-oriented context. No completed viewer payment is needed to identify what the video promotes.

citations.quote: so u also try to make such income SO CALL ME, MAIL ME

opening.argument: The visible transaction is a BUSD purchase form, not a demonstrated transfer to the speaker. A profile shows profits and counts for partners and team members, but those headings alone do not show that a viewer's payment funds another person's earnings. The invitation to call or email is a solicitation for contact, not a request in the supplied speech for a password or credentials. The evidence supports a promotional discussion of joining and purchasing BUSD; it leaves the alleged commission mechanism unshown.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening infers a tiered recruitment mechanism from proximity: partner and team counts appear near profits, and the speaker invites contact. That combination raises a question, but the displayed fields do not specify commission rules or show a downline payment. The later form concerns buying BUSD; the sampled frame does not show a completed purchase or where any purchased funds go.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The case does not depend on seeing a completed transfer or credential request. The title promotes joining Forsage, the profile places profits alongside partner and team metrics, and the speaker links a claimed income figure to an invitation to try and make similar income and contact them. The BUSD purchase screen reinforces the participation context; calling it an ordinary purchase does not account for the recruitment and earnings pitch around it.
